doc.title: Jones Hank — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: The Fats Waller album and Abbey Lincoln, via Jean-Philippe Allard
summary: Allard of French Verve put together the Waller project and 'Bug Waltz' with Abbey Lincoln as well as the Haden spirituals CD.

story.theme_name: Singers and the musicians who accompanied them

blocks.x: You mentioned Waller, which, in the 70s, became a very prominent player. I look to recordings, and I see when you are growing up and I wish there was a piano here so I could ask you to play the “Bug Waltz.” That's like my favorite tune of all time.
Yeah! I did a Fats Waller album later on for Verve. That was one of the tunes I did on there.
He also recorded that with Abbey Lincoln.
That's right. I think that was just the two of us.
That is a CD I play over and over again.
Well, Jean Filipe Allard was A&R man representing French Verve. He put that together. By the way, Abbey Lincoln, and she speaks French fluently. I think she did one of the tunes in French.
Yes she did. I can hear it now (sings in French).
She does great lyrics. In fact she writes complete songs. She's very talented woman.
How did that record come about?
It was his idea? Did he put the two of you together?

Yes, he did. Of course he was on the date Charlie Haden and I together to do that CD we did. We had done the concert in Montréal and it seemed to work doing both spirituals and jazz. So he said, "Let's do that on a recording."
So, did you… This is really digressing but, have you had a close relationship with him as a producer? Did he bring new project ideas?
At the time, yes. But, of course, I'm not recording for Verve anymore. I think he is still with the company but I understand he is with a different department

there. We are not in touch. It is a very large company so he's involved in some other kind of work. He might still be interested in doing things with Abbey Lincoln because she was one of his pet projects, you know? She is done a number of things with them.
